                       STIPULATION TESTIMONY OF JONATHAN LY

 1   Introduction

 2   Q     PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME AND BUSINESS ADDRESS.

 3   A     Jonathan Ly, 14323 S. Outer 40 Rd., Suite 206N, St. Louis, Missouri 63017.


 4   Q     ARE YOU THE SAME JONATHAN LY WHO PREVIOUSLY SUBMITTED DIRECT

 5         TESTIMONY IN THIS PROCEEDING ON BEHALF OF OCCIDENTAL PERMIAN

 6         LTD. (OPL)?

 7   A     Yes.


 8   Purpose

 9   Q     WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR TESTIMONY?

10   A     I am providing testimony in support of the Comprehensive Stipulation (Stipulation)

11         submitted on June 22, 2026, by: Southwestern Public Service Company (SPS); New

12         Mexico Department of Justice; New Mexico Large Customer Group; Louisiana Energy

13         Service, L.L.C. ; Federal Executive Agencies; Targa Resource Corp.; Walmart, Inc.;

14         Coalition for Clean Affordable Energy; Prosperity Works, and OPL. The Commission

15         Utility Division Staff is not a signatory to the Stipulation, but it does not oppose parts

16         of the Stipulation. The New Mexico Energy, Minerals and Natural Resources

17         Department takes no position on the Stipulation.


18   Assessment

19   Q     WHAT ISSUES DOES THE STIPULATION RESOLVE?

20   A     The Stipulation resolves issues related to SPS’s overall revenue requirement, class

21         cost allocation, class revenue allocation, and rate design.




                                            J.POLLOCK
                                            INCORPORATED
                                                                                  Jonathan Ly
                                                                                 Stipulation
                                                                                 Page 2

 1   Q    WHAT IS YOUR ASSESSMENT OF THE STIPULATION?

 2   A    The Stipulation provides a fair, just, and reasonable resolution to the issues related to

 3        the previously identified topics. The stipulated revenue requirement will allow SPS to

 4        continue providing safe and reliable electric service to its customers. In addition, the

 5        Stipulation’s revenue allocations will ensure that costs are reasonably assigned to,

 6        and recovered from, SPS’s various New Mexico retail rate classes.


 7   Revenue Requirement

 8   Q    DOES THE STIPULATION RESOLVE OPL’S CONCERNS REGARDING CERTAIN

 9        REVENUE REQUIREMENT ISSUES?

10   A    Yes.   Generally speaking, the $90.0 million stipulated base revenue increase is

11        significantly below SPS’s originally requested $175.3 million increase. More

12        specifically, the Stipulation addresses the concerns raised in OPL’s direct testimony

13        regarding: the deferred tax asset (DTA) associated with solar production tax credits

14        (PTCs); investment tax credits (ITCs) associated with SPS’s battery energy storage

15        systems (BESSs); tax credit transfer costs; deferral mechanisms; and excess liability

16        insurance (ELI) expense recovery. These concerns were addressed by my colleague,

17        Billie S. LaConte.


18   Q    PLEASE DESCRIBE THE RESOLUTION RELATED TO THE DEFERRED TAX

19        ASSET ASSOCIATED WITH SPS’S SOLAR PRODUCTION TAX CREDITS.

20   A    Under the terms of the Stipulation, SPS will be permitted to earn a return on the DTA

21        associated with the solar PTCs at its cost of long-term debt. This represents a

22        reasonable compromise between the full weighted average cost of capital requested

23        by SPS and the cost of short-term debt recommended by OPL.




                                           J.POLLOCK
                                           INCORPORATED
                                                                             Jonathan Ly
                                                                            Stipulation
                                                                            Page 3

 1   Q   HOW WILL INVESTMENT TAX CREDITS ASSOCIATED WITH SPS’S BATTERY

 2       ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEM RESOURCES BE TREATED?

 3   A   ITCs associated with Cunningham 1 BESS and Plant X BESS will be amortized over

 4       five years to reduce SPS’s revenue requirement, which is largely consistent with its

 5       request.


 6   Q   WILL SPS BE PERMITTED TO EARN A RETURN ON THE INVESTMENT TAX

 7       CREDIT TRANSFER COSTS AT ITS WEIGHTED AVERAGE COST OF CAPITAL

 8       AS IT PROPOSED?

 9   A   No, not in this proceeding. However, the parties agree that SPS may apply to earn a

10       return on these costs in a later proceeding.


11   Q   HOW WILL SPS RECOVER THE TRANSFER COSTS FOR PRODUCTION TAX

12       CREDITS FROM HALE AND SAGAMORE?

13   A   The transfer costs for PTCs from Hale and Sagamore will be recovered through the

14       Fuel and Purchased Power Cost Adjustment Clause (FPPCAC), as requested by SPS.


15   Q   PLEASE DESCRIBE HOW SPS’S REQUESTED DEFERRAL MECHANISMS ARE

16       ADDRESSED IN THE STIPULATION.

17   A   SPS requested the continuation of three deferral mechanisms: 1) ELI expenses

18       approved in Case No. 25-00030-UT; 2) investment in legacy meters approved in Case

19       No. 22-00178-UT; and (3) and Community Solar program costs approved in Case No.

20       23-00071-UT. The parties agree that SPS should be authorized to continue recovering

21       these previously approved mechanisms.




                                         J.POLLOCK
                                         INCORPORATED
                                                                                 Jonathan Ly
                                                                                Stipulation
                                                                                Page 4

 1                Additional trackers initially requested by SPS are withdrawn. Specifically, SPS

 2         withdrew its request for both the property tax tracker and continuation of its ELI

 3         expense tracker.


 4   Q     OVER WHAT PERIOD OF TIME WILL DEFERRED EXCESS LIABILITY

 5         INSURANCE EXPENSE BE AMORTIZED?

 6   A     The stipulating parties agree that deferred ELI expenses approved in Case No. 25-

 7         00030-UT should be amortized over three years. This period represents a middle

 8         ground between the two-year amortization requested by SPS and the four-year

 9         amortization recommended by OPL.


10   Class Cost Allocation

11   Q     DOES THE STIPULATION RESOLVE OPL’S CONCERNS REGARDING CERTAIN

12         COST ALLOCATION ISSUES?

13   A     Yes. The Stipulation specifically addresses OPL’s concerns about how SPS applied

14         the Average and Excess Demand – Four Coincident Peak (AED-4CP) method, the

15         treatment of behind-the-meter generation (BTMG), and PTC allocation.


16   Q     HOW WILL THE AED-4CP ALLOCATOR BE CALCULATED AND APPLIED

17         UNDER THE TERMS OF THE STIPULATION?

18   A     The signatory parties agree that the AED-4CP allocator should be calculated using

19         SPS’s annual system peak (1CP) demand and the system-wide load factor, consistent

20         with OPL’s recommendation. In addition, the AED-4CP allocator will be used to

21         allocate the costs of all production and transmission plant, including Hale and

22         Sagamore. This allocation, also consistent with OPL’s recommendation, is a change




                                           J.POLLOCK
                                          INCORPORATED
                                                                                Jonathan Ly
                                                                               Stipulation
                                                                               Page 5

 1        from SPS’s proposal under which the costs associated with Hale and Sagamore would

 2        have been allocated on an energy basis.


 3   Q    PLEASE DESCRIBE HOW THE STIPULATION ADDRESSES THE ISSUE OF

 4        BEHIND-THE-METER GENERATION.

 5   A    SPS agrees to study the impact on its wholesale and retail jurisdictions of excluding

 6        BTMG from its AED-4CP transmission allocators as part of its cost allocation

 7        workshops agreed upon in Case No. 25-00085-UT. The results of this study will be

 8        included in its next base rate filing.


 9   Q    HAVE THE PARTIES REACHED AN AGREEMENT ON THE ALLOCATION OF

10        PRODUCTION TAX CREDITS?

11   A    Yes. The parties agree that PTCs will be allocated to rate classes based on energy,

12        as recommended by OPL.


13   Class Revenue Allocation

14   Q    DOES THE STIPULATION PROVIDE FOR A REASONABLE CLASS REVENUE

15        ALLOCATION AMONG THE CUSTOMER CLASSES?

16   A    Yes. The stipulated class revenue allocation is summarized in Table 1 on the following

17        page. It is the product of negotiation and compromise between the parties. Although

18        some customer classes will receive below-average base rate increases, others will

19        receive above-average base rate increases — ultimately, however, the settlement

20        increase will be spread so that each customer class moves closer to cost.




                                             J.POLLOCK
                                             INCORPORATED
                                                                               Jonathan Ly
                                                                              Stipulation
                                                                              Page 6

                                             Table 1
                              Stipulation Class Revenue Allocation
                                                                Base Rate
                                 Customer Class                  Increase
                     Residential                                    17.50%
                     Small General Service                          17.50%
                     Irrigation Power Service                       10.39%
                     Secondary General Service                      17.02%
                     Primary General Service                        10.42%
                     Large General Service-Transmission             10.39%
                     Small Municipal and School                     18.01%
                     Large Municipal and School                     18.01%
                     Municipal Street Lighting                      17.15%
                     Area Lighting                                  18.27%
                        Total NM Retail                             12.55%

 1        These results are within the range of the recommendations from various parties; thus

 2        the outcome is informed by each party’s respective positions on cost allocation.

 3        Importantly, no class will receive a base rate increase less than 50% (6.28%) or more

 4        than 150% (18.83%) of the New Mexico retail average base rate increase. These

 5        results are consistent with the Commission’s long-standing principle of gradualism to

 6        avoid rate shock.


 7   Rate Design

 8   Q    IS SPS STILL REQUESTING APPROVAL TO RECOVER THE COSTS OF SPP

 9        DEFICIENCY PAYMENTS THROUGH THE FPPCAC?

10   A    No. SPS has withdrawn (without prejudice) its request to recover SPP deficiency

11        payments through the FPPCAC. Instead, The Stipulation terms state that SPS will

12        use its best efforts to address short-term capacity needs. To the extent SPS incurs

13        costs for deficiency payments, or for short-term capacity purchases to meet its



                                          J.POLLOCK
                                          INCORPORATED
                                                                                Jonathan Ly
                                                                               Stipulation
                                                                               Page 7

 1        capacity need, SPS may defer these costs in a regulatory asset for which it may seek

 2        cost recovery in a future proceeding, subject to an annual cap of $10 million and the

 3        right of parties to take any position regarding the recovery or reasonableness thereof.


 4   Q    HOW WILL OFF-SYSTEM SALES MARGINS FROM THE CUNNINGHAM AND

 5        PLANT X SOLAR PROJECT BE TREATED?

 6   A    SPS will be permitted to retain all off-system sales margins from the Cunningham and

 7        Plant X Solar Projects and Cunningham 1 BESS from the commercial operation date

 8        of these plants until cost recovery from customers commences. Once cost recovery

 9        for these projects from customers commences, SPS will credit customers with all off-

10        system sales margins, as recommended by OPL.


11   Conclusion

12   Q    WILL THE STIPULATION BENEFIT ALL OF SPS’S CUSTOMERS?

13   A    Yes. The Stipulation is the result of many hours of negotiation between parties with

14        competing interests and will benefit all parties fairly.


15   Q    DOES     THIS     CONCLUDE        YOUR      TESTIMONY      IN   SUPPORT     OF    THE

16        STIPULATION?

17   A    Yes.
